data.title_original: Sponsors’ health-related messaging & corporate social responsibility: a multi country analysis of the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games
data.abstract_original: Research Aim: This paper extends Furtado et al. (2025)’s exploration of health-related messaging before and during the 2024 Paris Olympic and Paralympic Games. Given that the overwhelming majority (95%) of that study’s health-related messages emanated from corporations, this paper aims to explore the confluence of health messaging with sport mega event (SME) sponsorship and corporate social responsibility (CSR). More specifically, this paper aims to categorise the types of health messaging and activations by national and transnational sponsors accredited through individual National Olympic Committees (NOC) and The Olympic Partner (TOP) programme. Our focus on health adds original contributions to the extant literature on leveraging sport sponsorship as a strategic component of CSR (McCullough and Trail, 2023; Uhrich et al., 2014).

data.title_original: Public Perceptions of Disability and Para Athletes Before and After the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games: An Exploratory Independent-Samples Study
data.authors: Pierre-Olaf Schut, Argenis Peniel Vergara-Torres, Athanasios Sakis Pappous
data.abstract_original: The Paralympic Games are frequently promoted as a catalyst for social change, yet evidence regarding their social legacy remains limited and inconclusive. This study examined differences in French public perceptions of disability before and after the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games using an independent-samples pre–post design. Two surveys were administered to French adults one month before the Games (Time 1: n = 948; Mage = 36.43 years, SD = 13.67) and approximately two months after the Games (Time 2: n = 930; Mage = 37.40 years, SD = 11.83). The questionnaire assessed general perceptions of disability, perceptions of Para athletes, perceived sporting and professional capabilities of persons with physical and vision impairments, and perceived improvements in public accessibility. Participants surveyed after the Games reported higher scores on general disability perceptions, perceptions of Para athletes, and perceptions of persons with physical disabilities. In contrast, lower scores were observed on four of five items concerning persons with vision impairments. Participants with a disability and those with a close personal connection to disability also reported more positive perceptions of public accessibility after the Games. These findings suggest that public perceptions differed before and after the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games but varied by disability type. Given the independent-samples design, they should be interpreted cautiously.

data.title_original: From outputs to outcomes? Examining the evolution of social impact reporting in UK major sport events [Abstract]
data.authors: James Andrew Kenyon, Jessica Padley, Viola Lyu, Peter Dickenson, Verity Postlethwaite
data.abstract_original: Aim and Research Questions This research examines how social impact claims and reporting practices are constructed, evidenced, and evolved within documentary materials relating to major sport events in the UK across four cycles aligned to the Rio (2013 - 2016), Tokyo (2017 - 2021), Paris (2022 - 2024), and Los Angeles (2025 - present) Olympic and Paralympic Games. It asks: 1. How are social impact claims constructed and evidenced within major sport event reporting across the four cycles? 2. What content trends and changes occur across cycles? The project frames these questions as an opportunity to demonstrate how a Theory of Change (ToC) approach can strengthen evidential claims, support longitudinal assessment, and encourage more policy relevant, equitable reporting.

data.title_original: Paralympic sport in Central Asia: a scoping review with descriptive analysis of participation, achievement, and medal efficiency (1996–2024)
data.abstract_original: Published research on Paralympic sport in Central Asia remains limited despite the region's growing presence at the Games. This review focuses on elite, Games-level participation and achievement. We conducted a scoping review reported in line with the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews, alongside an analysis of International Paralympic Committee (IPC) archival data for five Central Asian countries (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan) across Summer (1996–2024) and Winter (1994–2026) Games, framed through the SPLISS model and the constraint-led approach. The scoping review maps international knowledge; the IPC analysis documents regional outcomes, offering complementary evidence. The review identified three domains: income-, gender-, and technology-linked participation gaps (D1); discipline-specific age profiles ranging from a median of 25 years in Para Swimming to 38 years in Para Equestrian (D2); and ten national policy factors linked to Paralympic success (D3). IPC data showed Central Asian participation rising from 15 athletes in 1996 to 113 in 2024, led by Uzbekistan ( n = 64, Paris 2024) and Kazakhstan ( n = 44), concentrated in Para Athletics, Para Judo, and Para Powerlifting, plus a full Kazakhstani sitting volleyball squad and Para Swimming. Female representation rose from 0% in 1996 to 41.6% in 2024, near the ∼43% global benchmark. Medal efficiency was 0% before 2012, spiked to 73.5% at Rio 2016 (95% CI 59.7%–83.8%), driven by Uzbekistan winning more medals than athletes that edition, then settled at 32.9% (Tokyo 2020) and 31.0% (Paris 2024, 95% CI 23.2%–40.0%); the 2016 spike is statistically distinguishable from other editions, while Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 are not. Uzbekistan grew from 0 athletes in 1996 to 64 in 2024, with the sharpest rise from 32 (Rio 2016) to 64 (Paris 2024), coinciding with documented 2019–2024 state Paralympic-development measures-a plausible institutional account alongside classification reform and host-proximity effects. No study identified by our search has examined elite Paralympic sport development in Central Asia specifically. Four research priorities are proposed: epidemiological profiling, adapted policy analysis with regional researchers, longitudinal athlete tracking, and psychological support programs.

data.title_original: Historical and Contemporary Functions of Rituals in the Olympic Games
data.authors: Nurettin Göksu Çini, Suzan Dal, Selin Baikoğlu
data.abstract_original: The Olympic Games represent a multidimensional structure in which rituals, symbols, and ceremonial practices occupy an important place alongside athletic competition. In the Ancient Olympic Games, sacred processions, oaths, offerings, sacrifices, and award practices constituted important elements of the religious and social order. In the Modern Olympic Games, the Olympic rings, the flame and torch relay, the oath, and the opening, closing, and medal ceremonies are among the fundamental components of the symbolic and institutional structure of the Olympic Movement. This study aims to evaluate the rituals associated with the Olympic Games in terms of the functions they perform within the Games, rather than limiting the discussion to their historical development or to formal similarities and differences between the Ancient and Modern Olympics. Designed as a narrative review, the study examines historical and classical sources, academic studies, and institutional documents of the International Olympic Committee. Based on the evaluation of the literature, the functions of Olympic rituals were examined under five interrelated dimensions: the production of sacredness and meaning; regulatory, normative, and institutional functions; the formation of unity and belonging; the ritualization of achievement and honor; and the representation and visibility of Olympic values. The findings indicate that, in the Ancient Olympic Games, rituals contributed to maintaining the sacred order, reinforcing behavioral norms, and publicly honoring athletic achievement, whereas in the Modern Olympic Games they serve to sustain institutional order, symbolically reinforce a shared sense of belonging, ceremonially recognize achievement, and make Olympic values visible. In conclusion, Olympic rituals can be regarded not merely as ceremonial elements accompanying the Olympic Games, but as interrelated and multifunctional practices that contribute to the construction and maintenance of the Games’ worlds of meaning, order, belonging, achievement, and values.

data.title_original: Sex Differences in Injury, Stoppage and Concussion Rates in Amateur and Olympic-Style Boxing
data.abstract_original: Background. Women have boxed at the Olympic Games since 2012; since 2013 elite men have competed without headguards while women have kept them. Sex differences in injury, stoppage and concussion rates in amateur and Olympic-style boxing have not been systematically reviewed. The review question was: in amateur and Olympic-style boxers, do injury incidence, stoppage rates and concussion rates differ between women and men? Methods. PubMed/MEDLINE and Consensus were searched on 29 September 2026 (English-language reports, no date limit), with backward citation searching. Eligible studies reported at least one outcome (injury, stoppage, diagnosed concussion, laceration, fracture, other craniofacial or regional injury, or acute neurocognitive change) for women and men from the same amateur or Olympic-style boxing population with sex-specific denominators; outcomes were kept separate. Screening and extraction were single-reviewer with verification. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-E and certainty with GRADE. Risk ratios (women versus men) were pooled with a restricted maximum likelihood random-effects model with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Results. From 416 unique database records and 36 citation-search records, four studies were eligible, all International Olympic Committee injury-surveillance cohorts (Olympic Games 2012, 2016 and 2020; Youth Olympic Games 2018). Sex-specific boxing data were available from the published text of two. At London 2012, where both sexes wore headguards, 7 of 36 women (19.4%) and 18 of 247 men (7.3%) sustained a medical-attention injury (risk ratio 2.67, 95% CI 1.20 to 5.94). At Tokyo 2020, where men boxed without headguards and women with them, the reported risk ratio was 0.43 (0.24 to 0.75). The pooled estimate (risk ratio 1.05) was not interpretable (I² = 92%; Hartung-Knapp 95% CI 0.00 to >1000). The review question was: in amateur and Olympic-style boxers, do injury incidence, stoppage rates and concussion rates differ between women and men? Methods. PubMed/MEDLINE and Consensus were searched on 29 September 2026 (English-language reports, no date limit), with backward citation searching. Eligible studies reported at least one outcome (injury, stoppage, diagnosed concussion, laceration, fracture, other craniofacial or regional injury, or acute neurocognitive change) for women and men from the same amateur or Olympic-style boxing population with sex-specific denominators; outcomes were kept separate. data.title_original: Introduction: Rivalry, Recognition, and Soft Power in Sport Diplomacy
data.abstract_original: Sport diplomacy scholarship has continued to grow in recent years. This new literature builds on earlier ideas but moves beyond the studies as a battle between superpowers or the hosting of mega-events. Moving beyond these countries to consider regional rivalries, minority or oppressed groups, and middle powers brings greater insight into sport diplomacy and how it has functioned, particularly as a form of soft power. The Olympic movement and football are still important within sport diplomacy, but their examination from states other than the dominant countries provides more nuanced understanding. In addition, newer sport diplomacy scholarship incorporates different countries and sports, and increasingly considers women athletes and teams as important actors within sport diplomacy.

data.title_original: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research on Crowds and Disasters: A Vosviewer-Based Study Using the Scopus Database
data.abstract_original: Crowds are defined as situations in which large numbers of individuals congregate in close proximity. These environments can be observed in everyday settings such as shopping malls and metro stations, as well as planned events like football matches and the Olympic Games. In such settings, physical closeness, lack of social distancing and insufficient hygiene may pose significant public health and safety risks. When not properly managed, crowds can harm large numbers of people and exacerbate the impacts of existing disasters. The relationship between crowds and disasters is critical to risk assessment and crisis management. This study aims to conduct a bibliometric analysis of research within the context of crowds and disasters by examining documents indexed in the Scopus database using the keywords “crowd and disaster”. Bibliometric visualizations were generated using VOSviewer software. The analysis revealed that the most frequently used keywords were disaster management, crowd disasters, crowdsourcing, social media, and disaster response. In more recent years, keywords such as metro station, crowd evacuation, emergency evacuation, crowd disasters and stampede have gained prominence. It was also found that studies in this area spanned multiple disciplines, notably computer science, engineering, and the social sciences. Based on the findings, three research recommendations are proposed: fostering interdisciplinary collaboration, enhancing international cooperation and promoting research on crowds and disasters.

data.title_original: Age-Related Performance in Taekwondo Athletes with Physical Disabilities: An Analysis of the Paralympic Games
data.authors: Rafael Kons, Gennaro Apollaro, Matías Henríquez, María Isabel Cornejo, Vinicius de Oliveira Gulias, Daniele Detanico
data.abstract_original: Abstract This study investigated age-related performance in Para taekwondo athletes across two Paralympic Games editions, Tokyo 2020 + 1 and Paris 2024, examining potential differences according to Paralympic edition, sex, and competitive achievement. Data were obtained from the official results books of the Paralympic Games and included 192 Paralympic participation records, comprising 95 female and 97 male records. Age-related performance was analyzed according to Paralympic edition, sex, and competitive achievement, classified as medallist or non-medallist. Mann–Whitney U tests were used to compare age differences between groups, while chi-square (χ²) tests of independence were applied to examine the distribution of athletes across age categories (≤ 20, 21–25, 26–30, and ≥ 31 years). Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Female athletes were younger than male athletes at Paralympic participation (26 vs. 28 years; U = 3765.00, p = 0.028). No significant differences were observed between Paralympic editions (27 years for both; U = 4128.50, p = 0.653) or between medallists and non-medallists (26 vs. 28 years; U = 3395.50, p = 0.053). The distribution of athletes across age groups was similar for both sexes (χ²(3) = 5.71, p = 0.126) and competitive achievement levels (χ²(3) = 4.89, p = 0.180). Age differed by sex, whereas no significant age differences were observed according to competitive achievement or Paralympic edition. Overall, the age profile of Para taekwondo athletes at the Paralympic Games was concentrated in the late twenties, with female athletes showing a younger age profile than males, suggesting a consistent age pattern in this Paralympic combat sport.

data.title_original: Pathways to the podium: age and technical-tactical factors associated with medalling in Para Judo
data.abstract_original: This study aimed to explore factors associated with medalling in Para judo at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games, focusing on athlete characteristics and technical-tactical variables. Using published competition results, medalling outcomes for men and women were separately modelled using Bayesian penalised regression. Models included age, body weight, sport class, throws, groundwork techniques, and penalties per match. Results are reported as posterior probabilities that the regression coefficient was greater or less than zero, Pr(β > 0) or Pr(β < 0), according to the direction of the posterior mean. In males, age showed a predominantly negative posterior distribution (Pr[β < 0] = .944), whereas body weight (Pr[β > 0] = .972), throws (Pr[β > 0] >.999), groundwork techniques (Pr[β > 0] >.999), and penalties (Pr[β > 0] = .962) showed predominantly positive posterior distributions. In females, throws and groundwork techniques showed positive associations with medalling (both Pr[β > 0] >.999), whereas age (Pr[β < 0] = .818) and penalties (Pr[β < 0] = .801) showed predominantly negative posterior distributions with greater uncertainty. Overall, throws and groundwork techniques showed the most consistent positive associations with medalling across both sex-specific models. These findings may inform technical-tactical priorities and long-term athlete development in Para judo.

data.title_original: Adaptive Sports and Social Reintegration
data.abstract_original: Purpose: This study aimed to examine the role of participation in adaptive sports in the process of social reintegration among individuals with acquired physical disabilities, with a specific focus on para alpine skiing. Particular attention was given to the development of athletic identity and life satisfaction. Methods: This qualitative study formed part of a broader sequential mixed-method investigation. Following a quantitative phase involving 129 para alpine skiers, semi-structured interviews were conducted with six purposively selected elite para alpine skiers who participated in the Sochi 2014 Winter Paralympic Games to complement and deepen the quantitative findings. Data were analysed using qualitative content analysis informed by grounded theory principles, allowing for the identification of key categories and relationships within the resocialisation process. Results: The findings indicate that participation in adaptive sports, particularly para alpine skiing, plays a central role in social reintegration after disability. Athletes reported significant improvements in life satisfaction, driven by increased independence, structured daily routines, and meaningful goal-oriented activity. The reconstruction of athletic identity emerged as a key mechanism underlying psychological adaptation, contributing to enhanced self-concept and self-efficacy. In addition, participation in adaptive sports facilitated the expansion of social networks and strengthened interpersonal relationships, supporting broader social reintegration. However, the process was influenced by contextual factors, such as financial constraints and access to sports infrastructure. Conclusions: Adaptive sports participation represents a critical pathway for social reintegration, promoting life satisfaction and athletic identity development among individuals with disabilities. These findings highlight the importance of reducing structural barriers and ensuring equitable access to sport as part of comprehensive rehabilitation strategies.

data.title_original: Prevalence and patterns of sports supplement use in elite wheelchair basketball players: an analysis based on the AIS framework
data.authors: David Romero-García, María Isabel Buceta-Toro, Sara Perpiñá-Martínez, María Miana, Isabel Sospedra, Aurora Norte, Eva Ausó, Ana Cifuentes, Sara Aprea-Moreno, Pablo Leardy Palencia, Santiago Delgado Ortiz, José Miguel Martínez-Sanz
data.abstract_original: Background Sports supplement use is widespread in elite sport, yet evidence regarding supplementation practices in Paralympic team sports remains limited. Wheelchair basketball players present specific physiological and contextual characteristics that may influence supplement use and its alignment with current scientific evidence. Methods A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted in 66 elite Spanish wheelchair basketball players (57 men and 9 women) from 10 first-division teams. Participants completed a validated questionnaire assessing self-reported sports supplement use, reasons for consumption, and sources of information. Supplements were classified according to the Australian Institute of Sport (AIS) framework based on scientific evidence and safety. Descriptive and exploratory analyses were performed to examine associations between self-reported sports supplement use and athlete characteristics, including sex, functional classification, and training profile. Results Overall, 72.7% of athletes reported current self-reported sports supplement use. Expressed as proportions of the entire sample ( n = 66), Group A products were consumed by 66.7% of athletes, Group B products by 31.8%, while no athletes reported using Group C (0%) or Group D (0%) substances. Protein supplements, creatine monohydrate, and caffeine were the most frequently consumed products. Supplement use patterns were generally similar across sex and functional classifications, although no statistically significant differences were observed. Conclusion Elite wheelchair basketball players show a high prevalence of self-reported sports supplement use, predominantly involving products currently classified within AIS Group A. While the primary use of Group A supplements reflects a high intake of products with established efficacy, actual evidence-based practice requires individualized evaluation, underscoring the importance of professionally guided nutrition strategies in Paralympic team sports.

data.title_original: Epidemiological profile of musculoskeletal injuries in professional kata athletes: a retrospective descriptive study
data.authors: سمیراء کامیابی, Shayan Shafiei Nikou, Mansour Sahebozamani, Parishad Askari Geravandi, Mohammad Alimoradi, Mohammad Alghosi, Ivana Banićević, Farzaneh Saki
data.abstract_original: Exposure-adjusted injury risk in high-intensity kata performance remains poorly characterized. This study quantified the incidence, distribution, and context of musculoskeletal injuries among professional kata athletes. In a retrospective descriptive study, 210 Iranian Super League athletes (104 males, 106 females; mean ± SD age 23.5 ± 4.7 years) completed a standardized interview and an injury record form adapted from the International Olympic Committee surveillance system. Exposure was expressed as athlete-minutes across an 86-day pre-competition phase and a 3-day competition phase. Injury incidence (events/1000 athlete-minutes) with 95% CIs was estimated via Poisson methods; incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were calculated using Poisson regression with an exposure offset. Pearson’s chi-square tests were used to investigate the relationship between sex and categorical injury variables, including injury type, nature, and anatomical area. Of the 210 athletes, 112 (53.3%) sustained 138 injuries during 7,380 athlete-minutes of exposure (training: 6795; competition: 585). The overall injury incidence was 18.7 per 1,000 athlete-minutes (95% CI: 15.71–22.05). Injury incidence was substantially higher during competition (95.4 per 1,000 athlete-minutes) than during training (12.1 per 1,000 athlete-minutes; IRR = 7.9, 95% CI: 5.61–11.08). Male athletes sustained 80 injuries (58.0%) and female athletes 58 (42.0%), with no statistically significant difference in injury incidence after adjustment for exposure (IRR = 1.1, 95% CI: 0.79–1.56). Overuse injuries predominated, with the shoulder (23.2%) and knee (22.5%) being the most frequently affected anatomical areas. Professional kata athletes experience a substantially higher injury incidence during competition than training when adjusted for athlete exposure. Overuse injuries primarily involve the shoulder and knee, reflecting the repetitive demands of kata. No statistically significant sex difference in injury incidence was detected after exposure adjustment. These findings support targeted workload management, shoulder–knee injury prevention, and continued injury surveillance.

data.title_original: Predictive Governance: The Management Dilemmas of AI-Driven Anti-Doping Education
data.authors: Zemikael Getu, Sisay Mengistu, Tefera Tadesse
data.abstract_original: The integration of artificial intelligence into anti-doping governance represents a paradigmatic shift from reactive enforcement to predictive regulation, yet the educational dimensions of this transformation remain critically under-theorized. This article addresses the immediate 2026 technological disruption in sports administration by developing a conceptual framework for understanding the management dilemmas inherent in AI-driven anti-doping education. Drawing on a policy analysis of institutional documents, regulatory frameworks, and emerging technological applications across European, North American, and Asian contexts, the study identifies three fundamental tensions: the paradox of personalization versus standardization in educational content delivery; the conflict between algorithmic efficiency and athlete autonomy in risk assessment; and the governance gap between technological capability and regulatory accountability. The analysis reveals that AI-enhanced anti-doping education operates within a predictive governance logic that prioritizes pre-emptive intervention over deliberative engagement, generating what we term "algorithmic compliance" rather than ethical internalization. The article proposes a reflexive governance framework that integrates technical innovation with participatory oversight, athlete-centred design principles, and regulatory coherence. Recommendations address the imperative for WADA and national anti-doping organizations to develop binding standards for AI transparency, athlete data rights, and human oversight mechanisms in educational interventions. The findings contribute to broader debates on the governance of algorithmic systems in sport and the preservation of athlete agency within increasingly datafied regulatory environments. The analysis proceeded through a three-phase analytical procedure—descriptive mapping, hybrid inductive–deductive thematic coding, and framework construction—applied to the 28 institutional and regulatory documents, the technological cases, and the regulatory frameworks described below.

The article proposes a reflexive governance framework that integrates technical innovation with participatory oversight, athlete-centred design principles, and regulatory coherence. Recommendations address the imperative for WADA and national anti-doping organizations to develop binding standards for AI transparency, athlete data rights, and human oversight mechanisms in educational interventions. The findings contribute to broader debates on the governance of algorithmic systems in sport and the preservation of athlete agency within increasingly datafied regulatory environments. The analysis proceeded through a three-phase analytical procedure—descriptive mapping, hybrid inductive–deductive thematic coding, and framework construction—applied to the 28 institutional and regulatory documents, the technological cases, and the regulatory frameworks described below.

data.title_original: From norms to practice: benchmarking International Sports Federations against the UN anti-corruption framework
data.abstract_original: Abstract International Sports Federations (ISFs) occupy a structurally unique position in the global governance landscape: private associations incorporated under Swiss civil law that simultaneously exercise binding transnational regulatory authority over their respective sports domains. While Swiss association law is the dominant legal form across the Olympic Movement, this sample is intentionally jurisdictionally diverse, spanning Swiss, German, British, and Malaysian entities. Since each of these jurisdictions is party to UNCAC, the UNODC benchmark applies consistently across the sample irrespective of where each federation is headquarted. Although the United Nations Convention Against Corruption (United Nations 2004) and a comprehensive suite of UNODC guidance instruments have established precise standards for private organisations, no systematic empirical study has evaluated the extent to which ISF anti-corruption frameworks reflect these standards. This study addresses that gap through a researcher-led normative document benchmarking study of six summer Olympic ISFs, selected across three governance tiers identified by the Association of Summer Olympic International Federations (ASOIF) governance assessment. Employing a 41-question, four-point scoring instrument derived directly from five UNODC source documents, the study evaluates each ISF’s publicly available governance instruments against eight dimensions: leadership commitment, risk assessment, prohibited conduct scope, financial integrity, conflict of interest management, reporting mechanisms, training and education, and enforcement architecture. The findings reveal a structural pattern of partial alignment: ISFs demonstrate reasonable policy coverage at the level of normative commitments but systematic deficiency at the operational and oversight levels. Most critically, all six federations exhibit a significant deficit of internal financial crime controls. This absence encompasses gaps in corruption risk assessment, post-employment restrictions, and the structural independence of investigatory functions. The study concludes with a typology of governance archetypes observable across the cohort and targeted policy recommendations grounded in the UNODC normative architecture.

data.title_original: Homo Olympicus: Olimpismo como instrumento de formação humana
data.authors: Luis Gustavo Maganhato, Rafael Ângelo Bunhi Pinto, Rui Anderson Costa Monteiro, Rodrigo Paiva
data.abstract_original: In Brazil, Physical Education training has historically favored biological and technicist approaches to the detriment of philosophical, sociological and humanistic foundations aimed at the integral understanding of the human being. In this context, Olympism, conceived by Pierre de Coubertin as a philosophy of life based on the balance between body, mind and spirit, presents itself as an important pedagogical possibility for contemporary physical education. This theoretical essay aimed to analyze the concept of Homo Olympicus in contemporary society and discuss how Olympic Education can contribute to human formation in the context of contemporary educational and school sport. It is a theoretical essay, with a qualitative approach and analytical-descriptive character, based on bibliographic review and documentary analysis. The theoretical path was structured from the category’s philosophy of education, sports pedagogy, corporeality, fair play, educational sport and the anthropological concepts of Homo Ludens, Homo Gymnasticus, Homo Sportivus and Homo Olympicus. The results indicate that Olympic Education expands the pedagogical possibilities of sport by overcoming the restricted logic of performance and hypercompetitiveness, valuing principles such as respect, friendship, cooperation, excellence and citizenship. It was also evidenced that informal fair play and the valorization of corporeality contribute to overcoming reductionist perspectives present in school Physical Education. It is concluded that Olympism can be understood as a philosophy of education and a formative instrument for the construction of critical, autonomous and socially committed subjects.

data.title_original: Tirzepatide in Sport after Inclusion in the WADA Monitoring Program: An Updated Narrative Review of Body Composition, Muscle Preservation and Potential Performance Implications
data.authors: Dominika Kochan-Olszewska, Małgorzata Witaszczyk, Alicja Sołtan, Natalia Wiktorzak, Julia Lipska, Jagoda Prządka, Longin Rudnicki, Jakub Pawlicki, Gracjan Koźma, Paweł Klimas, Justyna Laskus, Bartosz Gawior, Olga Stasiak, Marta Borkowska
data.abstract_original: Background: Tirzepatide, as a dual agonist of the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors, has become one of the most effective pharmacological therapies used to treat obesity and metabolic disorders. Growing interest in its potential use among physically active individuals and the inclusion of tirzepatide markers in the World Anti-Doping Agency’s (WADA) monitoring program for 2026 highlight the need to reassess the significance of this substance in sports. Aim: The aim of this study was to update the available data on tirzepatide in the context of sports. Material and methods: A narrative review of the current literature on tirzepatide, incretin receptor agonists and their use in the context of sports was conducted. The analysis included clinical trials, systematic reviews, publications on body composition, metabolism, and exercise adaptation, as well as WADA regulatory documents. Results: Tirzepatide effectively reduces body weight and improves metabolic parameters. However, available evidence mainly concerns individuals with obesity or type 2 diabetes, rather than athletes. Changes in lean body mass during therapy may be relevant for physically active individuals, especially in sports requiring high strength and power. Although weight reduction could be beneficial in weight-class sports. Further studies are needed to assess the long-term impact of tirzepatide on athletic performance and to address the ethical issues associated with its use. Conclusions: Tirzepatide currently has no proven effect on enhancing athletic performance. However, its impact on body weight and body composition may be important for athletes. The inclusion of tirzepatide in WADA’s monitoring program highlights the need for further research into its potential misuse, its effects on muscle, and the long-term consequences of its utilization in the athletic population.

data.title_original: Identidad de género y deporte: debate en X sobre la participación de Imane Khelif en los Juegos Olímpicos de París 2024
data.authors: Francisco José García-Ull, José María Lamirán-Palomares, Lucas Aguilera Bono
data.abstract_original: Purpose: This study analyses the polarisation of public discourse on the social network X (formerly Twitter) surrounding Algerian boxer Imane Khelif's participation in the Paris 2024 Olympic Games. The aim is to examine how different positions on gender identity, fairness and legitimacy in elite sport are constructed, disseminated and contested. Methodology: A total of 35,676 posts from 25,984 unique users were collected and analysed using the professional tool Tweet Binder during the period 27 July to 10 August 2024. Automated sentiment analysis based on natural language processing (NLP) was applied, classifying posts into four categories (positive, negative, neutral and undefined), supplemented by temporal, linguistic and key-actor analysis. Results: Significant polarisation was identified. Although positive posts outnumbered negative ones (18% versus 17%), critical publications generated twice as many impressions (194.8 million versus 93.3 million). Public figures such as Elon Musk and J.K. Rowling amplified the controversy with posts exceeding 670 million combined views. Activity peaks coincided with key events such as Angela Carini's withdrawal. Conclusions: Social media platforms function as spaces of symbolic confrontation where emotionally negative content achieves greater reach. Misinformation about the athlete's medical condition fuelled reductionist narratives. Digital discourse may influence future sports regulations on inclusion and fairness.

data.title_original: The Landscape of Doping in Indian Sports: Contemporary Challenges and Deliberations
data.abstract_original: The menace of doping in the Indian sporting ecosystem is well acknowledged, but the social ramifications of the process have not been explored in depth. The paper aims to reflect upon the intricate social dynamics of doping structured by various socio-economic factors, cultural narratives, and the widespread availability of doping substances. Through ethnographic fieldwork in western Uttar Pradesh (India), the study uncovers the practice of doping among junior athletes, a significant lack of awareness of anti-doping frameworks among junior/adolescent athletes and Athlete Support Personnel (ASP) regarding anti-doping policies. It highlights the crucial role of suppliers in fostering a dopogenic environment. The findings illustrate a concerning landscape where regulatory efforts and initiatives by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) in India encounter obstacles due to a deficiency in the reach of educational frameworks and a cultural perception of doping as a pathway to success. The paper advocates for an intersectional approach to anti-doping frameworks, stressing the importance of collaboration among stakeholders to cultivate a culture of fair play, particularly in India&s;s aspirations to host the 2036 Olympic Games.

data.title_original: The Biomechanical and Perceptual Impact of Breast Support during Riding and Running in Female Equestrians
data.authors: Lorna Cameron, Natalie Stones, Victoria J. Lewis, Emma Davies, Jenni L. Douglas, Christy Maddock, Katy Searle, Jenny Burbage
data.abstract_original: Popular among women, equestrian sport is the only sex-integrated Olympic sport, relying on interspecies communication between horse and rider. Despite extensive breast research in sport, equestrian research is limited. This study investigated the impact of bras on breast movement, comfort, and pain; rider position and asymmetry; and compared breast movement and pain in riding versus running. Participants (n = 21) rode a Racewood™ Equine Simulator (ES) in walk, trot, and canter and ran on a treadmill (TM) in four breast support conditions: everyday (EB), encapsulation sports bra (ESB), combination sports bra (CSB), and bare-breasted (BB). Markers were tracked by a Qualisys motion capture system, and relative breast displacement (RBD) in TM and ES was calculated, along with rider position during ES. Exercise-induced breast pain (EIBP) and bra comfort were measured on 0–100 visual analogue scales, and a survey on bra performance and aesthetics was completed. TM caused the highest EIBP (mm) (x̃ = 67.25, P < 0.001) and RBD (cm) (x̃ = 5.56, P < 0.001) in BB. A moderate positive association (rs(19) = 0.428, P < 0.001) was observed between EIBP and RBD, both of which were reduced by ESB (EIBP P < 0.001; RBD P < 0.002) and CSB (EIBP P < 0.001; RBD P < 0.001) in trot and TM. In trot, torso position improved in ESB (Z = −3.841, P < 0.001) and CSB (Z = −3.806, P < 0.001) compared to EB, and riders were most symmetrical in ESB. Bra comfort and preferences were idiosyncratic. Bra type meaningfully influenced EIBP, rider position, and symmetry. Future larger, longitudinal, field-based studies are warranted.

data.title_original: Sportswashing and the Paradoxes of CSR: A critical public relations model of elite sports philanthropy
data.authors: Mitchell John Hobbs, Juan Feng, Li Mei, Xiufang Li
data.abstract_original: This article revisits a foundational question in critical public relations (CPR): how do we distinguish corporate social responsibility (CSR) grounded in genuine public interests from CSR activities that are strategically mobilized for reputational advantage? It addresses this question by exploring sportswashing, conceptualized here as a reputational outcome of sports philanthropy, particularly the sponsorship of elite athletes. It analyzes this phenomenon through a case study of Australian mining magnate Gina Rinehart and her sponsorships of elite Olympic athletes. It identifies the earned media publicity generated from these sponsorships through qualitative content analysis of Australian newspapers. The findings show that this coverage overwhelmingly framed Rinehart as a benevolent benefactor of Olympic sport, associating her with charismatic athletes and more abstract constructs such as patriotism and national glory. Ultimately, the article develops a critical public relations model of sportswashing (CPRMS) intended as a theoretical disruption of uncritical accounts of CSR. This model demonstrates that sports philanthropy, while clearly beneficial to athletes, can also serve as a tool for image bolstering in the service of private capital.

data.title_original: Athlete gender visibility, emotional narratives, and audience engagement in CCTV News’s Olympic short-video coverage on Douyin: an empirical analysis
data.authors: Gengxin Yi, Feng Gao, Haojie Wang
data.abstract_original: Short-form video platforms have become important channels for major sports-event coverage, but empirical evidence remains limited regarding how athletes are presented, how emotions are organized, and how these features relate to audience engagement in specific institutional accounts. This study analyzes 219 short-video posts published by the official China Central Television (CCTV) News account on Douyin during the 2024 Paris Olympic Games. Content analysis, t-tests, and regression analysis were used to examine mention-based athlete gender visibility, emotional narratives, and three platform-displayed engagement indicators: likes, comments, and shares. The results show no statistically significant difference between female and male athletes in mention frequency, indicating relative balance only at the level of being named. Athlete mention frequency was not significantly associated with likes, comments, or shares. Emotional narratives were not directly associated with higher engagement, but posts using emotional narratives contained significantly more athlete mentions. Emotional narrative also positively moderated the relationship between mention frequency and shares, although not the relationships with likes or comments. These findings suggest that, within this single-account and single-platform case, mention frequency is a potential narrative resource rather than an engagement outcome in itself, and its association with content diffusion depends partly on emotional framing. The conclusions should not be generalized to all Chinese mainstream media or interpreted as evidence of complete gender equality in athlete portrayal.

data.title_original: A fada do skate e o empoderamento do mito: A perspectiva feminista na construção publicitária de Rayssa Leal durante as Olimpíadas de Tóquio 2020
data.authors: JÚLIA FERNANDA LEMOS BACKES, Gustavo Roese Sanfelice, Mauricio Barth
data.abstract_original: Rayssa Leal was only six years old when she was nicknamed "Fadinha" (Little Fairy), a moniker that bridged the playful world of children's stories with skateboarding and contributed to building her mythic image in the media landscape. Against this backdrop, this study analyzes the representation of the Brazilian athlete in advertising media related to the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games, viewed through the lens of female empowerment. To this end, the study employs the film analysis framework proposed by Vanoye and Goliot-Lété (2006), applying it to keyframes from the "Novas Fadas" (New Fairies) commercial produced by Nike. The theoretical framework integrates concepts of myth, advertising, and gender equity, while also addressing "Femvertising" and its implications for contemporary representations of women. The results indicate that the campaign constructs a mythic, inspirational image of Rayssa Leal through visual elements, animation, and soundtrack, reinforcing values ​​associated with overcoming obstacles and realizing dreams. Concurrently, the narrative mobilizes discourses regarding gender equality and the valuing of women's presence in historically male-dominated spaces, positioning the athlete as a symbolic figure of inspiration, representation, and social transformation.

data.title_original: Casting On at the Games: Knitting Through Milano Cortina
data.authors: Marja‐Leena Rönkkö, Anna Kouhia, Tellervo Härkki
data.abstract_original: This study examined how Olympic athletes shared knitting-themed content on Instagram before, during, and after the Milano Cortina Winter Games in early 2026, with particular attention paid to the themes associated with posts. Instagram has been recognized as a key platform for craft-related content among makers, and it has also served as a central space for athletes’ personal brand building. The research data were collected from athletes’ public Instagram accounts, including images and Reels, up to April 10, 2026, at which point several recurring narratives and themes reached a natural conclusion as the season ended. The findings suggest that athletes utilized social media to curate their personal brands. They framed knitting as a relaxing and enjoyable activity to balance intensive training schedules and traveling. Many emphasized the importance of finalizing knitting projects and described a sense of satisfaction and pleasure upon finishing them. A notable practice involved the “Knitting Club,” where athletes gathered face-to-face during the Olympic Games. Interaction between athletes and their followers was frequent, with numerous comments in the comment sections and shared challenges. Overall, the dialogue was predominantly positive and supportive, highlighting knitting as a means of expressing identity and building community in elite sports contexts.

data.title_original: Women's participation in the Paralympic Games (1960–2024): a longitudinal and bibliometric analysis of global trends and scientific production
data.authors: Renato De Donato, Chiara Milanese, Nicole Lorenzet, Federico Schena, Valentina Cavedon
data.abstract_original: Background Women's participation in the Paralympic Games has expanded over time, yet this growth has been non-linear and uneven across regions, disciplines, and editions. At the same time, scientific research on women in Paralympic and parasports contexts remains limited and geographically concentrated. Studies that provide a comprehensive, long-term, sex-disaggregated reconstruction of participation across both Summer and Winter editions, together with an examination of its relationship to the geography of scientific production, are scarce. Methods This study reconstructs sex-disaggregated participation in the Summer Paralympic Games (1960–2024) and Winter Paralympic Games (1976–2022) using official data provided by the International Paralympic Committee (IPC), harmonized with National Paralympic Committee data. Longitudinal trends and cross-national patterns are examined through descriptive and comparative analyses. Exploratory non-parametric analyses were used to assess longitudinal trends and macro-regional differences in demographic-normalized participation. As a complementary component, a systematic search of the Web of Science Core Collection (completed 31 October 2025) identified 71 relevant publications, which were analyzed using bibliometric techniques. Results Women's participation in the Summer Paralympics follows a non-linear trajectory, reaching near parity at Paris 2024 (44.4%), whereas participation in the Winter Games remains consistently lower, with only modest long-term growth and no comparable movement toward parity (18%–25%). Two study-specific descriptive indicators, i.e., the Weighted Equity Index and the Normalized Female Participation Index, were used to summarize cross-national differences in internal delegation balance and demographic-normalized participation intensity. The bibliometric analysis documents a small but expanding body of literature that is geographically concentrated. Conclusion These findings suggest a persistent misalignment between the increasing presence of women in the Paralympic Games and the comparatively limited and uneven development of scientific research on this population. The study provides a comprehensive longitudinal mapping of women's participation and offers an empirical basis for future research and policy aimed at improving equity in Paralympic sports.

data.title_original: AN INTEGRATED MULTI-INSTRUMENT FRAMEWORK FOR OPERATIONAL AVALANCHE RISK MANAGEMENT: THE MILANO CORTINA 2026 WINTER OLYMPICS IN LIVIGNO, ITALY
data.authors: Fabiano Monti, Alberto Mariani, Martin Metzger, Luca Dellarole, Giacomo Villa, Diana Lazzeri
data.abstract_original: Avalanche risk management in complex alpine environments increasingly relies on the integration of heterogeneous data sources and modelling approaches into a coherent operational framework.During the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games, an advanced multi-layer system was implemented in Livigno (Italy) to support real-time decision-making for avalanche risk mitigation affecting critical infrastructures.The system combined in situ measurements and field observations, automatic detection technologies, numerical weather model (NWM) data, snowpack modelling and avalanche dynamics simulations within a unified operational environment.Automatic Weather Stations (AWS) provided continuous observations of key meteorological and snow variables, forming the basis for both process interpretation and model forcing.These data were complemented by NWM outputs, used both as forecast products and as input for snowpack simulations.Snowpack evolution was simulated using the SNOWPACK model, providing stratigraphic information, stability indices and forecasts of typical avalanche problems.These outputs were coupled with automated identification of Potential Release Areas (PRA) and avalanche dynamics simulations using the AvaFrame framework, together forming PRISM (Potential Release-area & Impact Scenario Modelling), which generates daily scenario-based maps of potential release and impact areas under different instability regimes.Automatic avalanche detection systems added a real-time observational layer: a geophone-based system with traffic-light control and an infrasound array enabled continuous (24/7) detection of avalanche events, even under poor visibility or during nighttime.High-resolution webcams supported rapid validation of detected events and enhanced situational awareness.Satellite-based SAR observations (Sentinel-1) provided spatially distributed evidence of avalanche activity and supported the identification of released slopes and residual hazard areas.All data streams were integrated into dedicated operational platforms, enabling real-time visualization, analysis and reporting.The strength of the approach lies in the synergy between complementary components: observations describe current conditions, models anticipate future evolution, and remote sensing validates spatial patterns.The system was successfully tested under critical conditions during February 2026, including periods of High avalanche danger (level 4 of 5), while simultaneously managing routine avalanche forecasting and risk mitigation activities typical of an inhabited alpine valley and ski resort, demonstrating the effectiveness of an integrated observation-modelling-decision framework for avalanche risk mitigation in high-stakes environments.

data.title_original: Poland's state capitalism, state dirigisme and the European Games
data.authors: Wojciech Woźniak, Radosław Kossakowski, Przemysław Nosal
data.abstract_original: This article examines Poland's organisation of the 2023 European Games as a case study of state capitalism and dirigisme under the Law and Justice (PiS) government. Drawing on qualitative analysis of official documents, public statements and media coverage, the study examines the political rationales, institutional arrangements and discursive justifications underpinning the decision to host the Games and the political processes surrounding the project. The study analyses how illiberal governance and centralised control were exerted as the showcase of the state’s dirigisme. It argues that the Games exemplified a politically driven megaproject shaped by the pursuit of the ‘political sublime’ – the symbolic display of state efficacy rather than pragmatic legacy goals. By situating the Polish case within broader debates on mega-events and public management, the article shows that even events of relatively limited global prominence can reproduce governance patterns typically associated with the ‘flagship’ sporting mega-events like the Olympic Games or FIFA World Cups. Additional context emphasising the role of the state’s dirigisme and political sublime of sporting events emerging from the analysis concerns the fact that all major political parties in Poland, otherwise bitterly conflicted, declare that pursuing the goal of hosting, for the first time, the Summer Olympic Games in Poland is a part of their political agenda.

data.title_original: Tennis as a Spark for Olympic Health Legacy in Developing Host Cities
data.authors: Yash Sharma, Sourav Ghosh, Priyanka Pandey
data.abstract_original: Tennis as a sport, with its accessibility and comprehensive health benefits, offers a strategic chance to amplify the Olympic health legacy, especially in developing host cities. By utilizing tennis beyond elite competition, cities can foster sustainable health improvements through inclusive infrastructure, community programs, and long-term engagement. This paper explores how tennis can contribute to physical, mental, and social well-being, while also promoting public health systems and urban development through Olympic legacy frameworks.

data.title_original: Fortifying the Arena: Multi-Layered Security Strategies for the 2036 Olympics in Ahmedabad
data.abstract_original: The Olympics and Indian Premier League (IPL), as mega-events important to the world due to their acknowledgment of athletic accomplishments and cultural cohesion, are situated to experience asymmetric and diverse threats and attacks as a result of their size and complexity. This paper examines global and technical propositions incorporated into security research, and states over fifty years of academic research and operational experiences with event and stadium security, including being an integral part of the managing of the security program at Wankhede Stadium for IPL seasons. This paper calls on the three-fold sections of security, an array of concepts, using evidence through observation and review of the mega-events of Olympic Games. This piece recommends a multi-faceted approach on behalf of the 2036 Olympics considering aspect of threat prevention, anticipating what innovation technology will be a consideration, the rapid-outlining of geospatial threat, and engaging with a stakeholders as organizations, the public and private sector professionals. In this paper is the managing and overview of formal strategies for resilience, external threat and vulnerability mitigations, as well as discussions on formal approaches urban planning, and forums designed to research a legacy of security. data.title_original: Hosting Olympic Games in Divided Nations During the Cold War Era: The Legacy of the 1972 Munich and 1988 Seoul Games
data.abstract_original: This study compares the 1972 Munich and 1988 Seoul Olympics—two Games hosted by divided nations aligned with the Western bloc during the Cold War. While each event has been extensively studied in isolation, comparative research remains limited. Using a three-level framework (national, interstate, international), this paper addresses that gap by analysing the motivations, the challenges and responses, and the legacies of both cases. Findings show how each nation used the Olympics to reshape its international image, assert legitimacy, and navigate Cold War tensions. Differences in political systems—bottom-up federal democracy in West Germany and top-down authoritarianism in South Korea—shaped contrasting approaches to planning and execution. The study argues that these Games were not the culmination of national development strategies, but rather transformative junctures that redefined political narratives, urban infrastructure, international standing, and sport science in each country. This analysis contributes to Olympic historiography and offers practical insights for contemporary nations considering Olympic bids amid ongoing domestic and geopolitical challenges.

data.title_original: From the Past to the Future: Environmental Legacies of the Olympic Games in a Warming World
data.abstract_original: Olympic Games are considered to be one of the most impactful mega-sports events taking place after every four years. The Olympic Games stimulate the economical, social and environmental conditions of cities all over the world. Recent Olympics in Paris in 2024 caused a carbon footprint of 1.59 million teqco2, an unbelievable reduction in 54.6 percent emission over London 2012 and Rio 2016 Games. The paper is a mixed-method study, which examines the environmental legacies of the Olympic Games based on secondary data. It covers the historical analysis, comparative assessment between host cities, and provides the information on climate-responsive policies. The results indicate considerable change in carbon footprints, noting that the emissions for the 2024 Paris Games were reduced compared to previous Games, however, issues, such as greenwashing and environmental impact of mega-events, remain the same; the study indicates the need for host cities, including developing countries like India and Indonesia, to create detailed sustainability mechanisms, which will increase the longevity and legacy of the Olympic Games in a warming planet.

data.title_original: India's Quest for Hosting 2036 Olympics: Benefits, Risks and Mitigation Strategies
data.abstract_original: The Olympic Games are the biggest sporting extravaganza and bring together billions of viewers while providing an opportunity for host nations to showcase their cultural and economic strengths. Hosting such an event presents a platform for increased economic growth, job creation, promoting tourism, and attracting foreign investment for host nations and cities. However, past host cities including Athens (2004), and Montreal (1976) have faced issues like financial burdens, unused infrastructure, and increasing debts. As India aspires to host the 2036 Olympics, this paper examines the challenges, risks, and proposes strategies necessary to host the games in a manner that&s;s economically sustainable and environmentally responsible. A narrative literature review was conducted followed by thematic analysis to assess India&s;s preparedness and propose recommendations for hosting the 2036 Olympics. It analyses secondary data sources, including reports from the International Olympic Committee (IOC), the Olympic Games Organizing Committees (OGOCs), as well as research papers and articles. The findings show that hosting the Games can have a positive impact on the economy as a result of increased tourism and foreign direct investment, generate employment opportunities, and support urban renewal through infrastructure development projects. Nonetheless, despite these potential benefits, it also poses risks like huge cost overruns, governance and corruption issues, the “white elephant phenomenon,” and security issues, all of which entail hefty costs. By employing strategic planning, promoting public- private partnerships, and strengthening governance, India can mitigate these risks and organise a successful Olympic Games that leaves a lasting legacy.

data.title_original: Assessing the Legacy Possibilities of the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games
data.authors: H. Bjorn Galjaardt, Stephen Townsend, John Cairney, Véronique Richard, Ian Jobling
data.abstract_original: The Summer Olympic Games have been held twice in Australia: 1956 in Melbourne and 2000 in Sydney. A third Olympic and Paralympic Games has been awarded to Brisbane in 2032. Using archival research which locates legacy in documents relating to both the 1956 and 2000 Olympics, this article considers how notions of legacy are being presented to the public in the years leading to Brisbane 2032. The term ‘legacy’ was first mentioned in the Melbourne candidature bid, and much more prominently in the Olympic Movement since Sydney 2000. Legacy is a result of vision, encompassing tangible and non-tangible benefits by hosting the Olympics. There are increased cultural, social, and political expectations to deliver more positive ‘legacies’ for host regions. This research also considers the role that Australia&s;s three International Olympic Committee sanctioned Centers for Olympic Studies can play in identifying and empowering opportunities for legacy creation in the lead up to the 2032 Games.

data.title_original: Avoiding White Elephants in Olympic Games: Lessons for India's 2036 Olympic Bid from Past Hosts
data.abstract_original: The problem of “white elephants”—costly, underutilized Olympic infrastructure—has imposed significant financial and social burdens on numerous host cities. This study employs a comparative case study methodology to examine the post-Games legacy of Athens 2004, Sochi 2014, Rio 2016, and London 2012, focusing on legacy planning, venue utilization, economic outcomes, and community integration. Data were collected from academic literature, International Olympic Committee reports, government documents, and evaluations to assess legacy outcomes across diverse economic and cultural contexts. Findings highlight London&s;s success through proactive legacy integration, temporary venues, and urban regeneration alignment, in contrast to Athens’ neglected venues, which are due to reactive planning. Sochi&s;s ambitious infrastructure faced sustainability challenges, while Rio achieved partial success through educational and transportation initiatives, despite political disruptions. For India&s;s 2036 Olympic bid, recommendations include early legacy planning, multi-purpose venue designs, public-private partnerships, and alignment with the Smart Cities Mission. By adopting digital platforms for transparent governance and community engagement, India can avoid white elephants and establish a global benchmark for sustainable Olympic hosting.

data.title_original: Turistična izkušnja in zadovoljstvo na mega-športnih dogodkih : študija primera zimskih olimpijskih iger Milano–Cortina 2026
data.abstract_original: This thesis examines tourist experience and visitor satisfaction at the Milano–Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games. The main aim of the study was to analyse how tourists evaluated their experiences during the event and to identify the factors that influenced their overall satisfaction. A qualitative research design was adopted, using qualitative content analysis of user-generated content based on 91 online visitor reviews collected from platforms including Google Maps, Reddit, YouTube, Business Insider, and Itinerant Fan. The findings indicate that most visitors evaluated their experience positively, highlighting the Olympic atmosphere, high-quality sporting competitions, natural Alpine scenery, volunteer support, the opportunity to explore different host destinations, and the opportunity to participate in winter sport activities themselves. At the same time, the study identified several organisational challenges related to transportation, accommodation, crowd management, food services, accessibility, and visitor information. The results demonstrate that tourist satisfaction at mega-sport events depends not only on the sporting programme but also on the quality of supporting tourism services and destination management. Based on the findings, practical recommendations are provided for organisers of future mega-sport events to improve visitor experience, event organisation, and the quality of tourism services.

data.title_original: Physical Disability Inclusion, Rights, and Representation in the North American Professional Sports Industry
data.abstract_original: This thesis focuses on the history of physical disability inclusion, rights, and representation in the North American professional sports industry, from the early 1980s to 2026 It examines progress and resistance in furthering disability inclusion and integration in the professional sports industry among athletes, team staff, and fans. The current literature on disability within the sports industry largely focuses on the Paralympics, which means there is a substantial gap in the sport management literature. This thesis contributes to filling that gap by examining disability in professional sport. This thesis argues that the professional sports world is a helpful stage to amplify and portray disability integration, inclusion, and accommodation for athletes, fans, and team personnel, while simultaneously revealing significant barriers that remain. This thesis concludes with a discussion of major areas of improvement to further address the needs and reality of the lived disability experience within the professional North American sports industry.

data.title_original: Quebec, pioneer of Olympic education: the little-known story of the 1976 Montreal Games
data.abstract_original: In the run-up to the 1976 Montreal Olympic Games, physical education in Quebec came under fierce criticism, with some even calling it a ‘disgrace.’ Based on this observation, this paper aims to analyze how the Olympic context served as a catalyst for redefining the role of physical education and sport in Quebec society, particularly in the field of education. The 1976 Montreal Olympic Games left a major educational legacy, often overshadowed by financial and organizational challenges. The ‘Promotion de l’Olympisme en Milieu Scolaire’ (Promotion of Olympism in Schools) program, the first of its kind, made history by integrating Olympic education into Quebec schools. Inspired by Pierre de Coubertin's humanistic vision, this program aimed to promote the values of sport and Olympism while improving the physical fitness of youth in Quebec. It served as a model for the Olympic Movement, which drew inspiration from it to develop similar initiatives on a global scale. The legacy of POMS lies in its innovative approach, combining physical education, Olympic values, and inclusion, and in its lasting impact on Quebec's sports and educational culture, which continues to this day.

data.title_original: Resolution of Human Rights Disputes Arising from Megasport Events: Why Claims Against Sport Governing Bodies Are Next to Impossible
data.abstract_original: Sport governing bodies (SGBs) such as FIFA and the International Olympic Committee absolve themselves of any liability under contract or tort from claims arising in connection with megasport events. They are able to do this by delegating all liability from potential claims to the MSE’s host state and its local organizing committee. As a result of these host state agreements, the host state will adopt enabling legislation and the SGB in question will be immune not only as a matter of contract, but also as a matter of law. This state of affairs is not satisfactory, chiefly because the SGB, as the superior negotiating party in host state agreements, has the power to impose stricter and more efficient procedures for access to justice as a form of responsibility incumbent on host states. Such responsibility may well include a rigid obligation to expeditiously and impartially subject relevant claims to standing or ad hoc judicial and arbitral bodies. In turn, these bodies must dispense justice in a manner that is consistent with fundamental human rights. This is something that SGBs have consciously failed to demand in host state agreements, thereby leaving claims by aggrieved parties unresolved or subjected to mechanisms that fail to deliver true justice. Therefore, it is imperative that the next generation of host state agreements engage with the needs of disadvantaged stakeholders and demand that host states adapt to higher standards of fair trial rights.

data.title_original: Sixteen Years Later: Revisiting Cultural Complexes and the Roots of Archetypal Thematic Analysis (ATA) 1
data.abstract_original: Abstract Written as a letter to my 28‐year‐old self, this paper explores the development of my engagement with cultural complexes . On August 18, 2009, I finished a chapter applying cultural complexes to a history of China, complete with elaborate charts that seemed to confirm a process by which cultural complexes are formed, and how China’s then recent actions during the Beijing Olympic Games (i.e., utilising 7‐year‐old Yang Peiyi’s vocals yet refusing to allow her to perform at the opening ceremony, opting instead for the lip‐syncing of 9‐year‐old Lin Miaoke and the initial cover‐up of classical dancer Liu Yan’s accident during rehearsals) seemed to confirm the constellation of emotional and behavioural patterns that could be usefully assembled under the concept. While this paper is an opportunity to reflect on my critical assessment of cultural complexes, it is equally an example of autoethnographic study and a meditation on personal archival practices within a post‐ and neo‐Jungian framework. Crucially, an autoethnographic approach has facilitated an understanding of how the development of archetypal thematic analysis (ATA) (in collaboration with Ann Yeoman) stems from my thinking around, and appraisal of, cultural complexes. ATA is offered as a complement to cultural complex theory (CCT) in the hopes that a mobilisation of both can produce a methodological expression of a ‘third way’ or what Paul Preciado calls a mutant psychoanalysis .

data.title_original: Avaliação da Satisfação dos Voluntários com as Iniciativas de Sustentabilidade nos Jogos Olímpicos de Paris 2024
data.authors: Risato Ando, Supitr Samahito, Jun Mitarai
data.abstract_original: This study examines volunteer satisfaction with the sustainability initiatives implemented during the Paris 2024 Olympic Games using the psychological constructs of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) as a theoretical framework. Rather than testing the original TPB model, the study investigates whether attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control are associated with satisfaction across seven sustainability dimensions: Carbon Neutrality, Renewable Energy, Public Transport, Waste Management, Sustainable Architecture, Social Inclusion, and Economic Sustainability. The results reveal that subjective norms were significant positive predictors across several sustainability dimensions, highlighting the importance of social expectations in shaping volunteer evaluations. Perceived behavioral control also showed significant positive associations, particularly with Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy, suggesting that volunteers who perceived greater ability to contribute reported higher satisfaction. However, lower explanatory power was observed for Public Transport and Social Inclusion, indicating that additional contextual factors may influence volunteer satisfaction. These findings demonstrate that TPB-derived psychological constructs provide a useful perspective for understanding volunteer evaluations of sustainability initiatives and offer practical implications for enhancing volunteer experiences in future mega-sport events, consistent with the sustainability objectives of Olympic Agenda 2020+5.

data.title_original: The Price of the Games—Or Whether Mega‐Sporting Events Improve Human Rights in the Host Country
data.abstract_original: ABSTRACT Objective The controversy surrounding the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar and the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States has renewed debate over whether hosting mega‐sporting events affects human rights. This article examines whether host governments strategically adjust civil liberties in response to international scrutiny. Methods Using a bidder‐based difference‐in‐differences design, it analyses 74 FIFA World Cups and Olympic Games (1900–2022), comparing successful hosts with unsuccessful bidders across nine civil liberties dimensions from the Varieties of Democracy (V‐Dem) dataset. Results The findings support a selective adjustment thesis. Seven dimensions show no statistically robust effects, suggesting that hosting does not systematically alter most civil liberties. Freedom from forced labor improves before events but deteriorates afterward, consistent with strategic reputation management. A marginal effect on freedom of religion does not survive multiple‐testing correction. Conclusions Host governments, therefore, appear to selectively manage internationally visible rights rather than undertake genuine human rights reform.

A marginal effect on freedom of religion does not survive multiple‐testing correction. Conclusions Host governments, therefore, appear to selectively manage internationally visible rights rather than undertake genuine human rights reform.

data.title_original: Evaluating the usability and practicality of a proposed carbon footprint methodology and tool for National Olympic Committees
data.abstract_original: Robust carbon footprint methodologies and tools are increasingly required across the sport sector, yet National Olympic Committees lack a standardised, sector-specific approach. A bespoke carbon footprint methodology and accompanying calculation tool were developed for this purpose; however, technical rigour alone does not ensure that intended users can apply them. This study evaluates the usability and practicality of the proposed methodology and tool through direct engagement with end-users. Fourteen staff members from different National Olympic Committees applied the methodology and tool within their organisations over a four-to-six-week period, then completed the System Usability Scale and a semi-structured interview. The tool achieved a mean System Usability Scale score of 68.4, corresponding to a grade C and a marginal-high acceptability rating. Usability was rated positively, whereas learnability scored below the neutral midpoint, and scores correlated strongly with participants' years of experience (r = .99). Interviews indicated that effectiveness was the strongest dimension and learnability the weakest, with data collection identified as the main source of effort. Participants judged the methodology rigorous and credible but recommended improved onboarding, validation, and guidance to support less experienced users and wider adoption.

data.title_original: Professionalization of coaches in performance-oriented sport for athletes with visual impairments: a qualitative study
data.authors: Ulrich Theobald, Tabea Nauschütz, Jonathan Knapp, Martin Giese
data.abstract_original: Introduction Coaching athletes with visual impairments (VI) involves distinct pedagogical, sport-specific, and organizational demands. However, research on the professionalization of coaches in Paralympic sport remains scarce. This study explores qualifications, experiences, attitudes, and contextual conditions relevant to coaching in this setting. Methods Semi-structured expert interviews were conducted with four experienced coaches working in blind football, goalball, judo, and rowing at a German Paralympic training center. Transcripts were analyzed using structuring qualitative content analysis with an inductive–deductive category-development approach. Results Five interrelated dimensions emerged: pathways and motivations for Paralympic coaching, qualifications and competencies, coaching philosophy, institutional conditions, and sport-specific adaptations. Formal qualifications provide an important basis, but disability-specific expertise was primarily acquired through practical experience and self-directed learning. Empathy, flexible communication, individualized motor-learning strategies, and trust-based yet performance-oriented coach athlete relationships were central to practice. Limited resources, informal entry pathways, and insufficient specialist education constrained professionalization. Conclusions Coaching in performance-oriented sport for athletes with VI requires more than theory-based licenses. Practice-oriented, disability- and sport-specific education, mentoring, and the systematic transfer of experiential knowledge are needed. Stronger institutional support and collaboration among schools, clubs, and federations may promote sustainable coaching structures and equitable athlete development in Paralympic sport.

data.title_original: The Influence of Sleep and Autonomic Recovery on Performance in World-Class Swimmers at Major Competitions: The Qualifying Trials, World Championships, and Olympic Games
data.authors: Lidia Barragán Hernández, Carmen Crespo, Sérgio J. Ibáñez, Rafael Timón, Guillermo J Olcina
data.abstract_original: Sleep deprivation is one of the main risk factors for impaired performance in elite athletes, but the changes in sleep and autonomic regulation in response to competitions of varying levels within the same Olympic year remain unknown. In this prospective, longitudinal, observational study, we monitored parameters related to sleep quality and quantity, as well as heart rate variability and resting heart rate, in a cohort of eight Olympic swimmers (n = 8) during the World Championships in Doha, the qualifying trials, and the 2024 Paris Olympic Games, using the Oura Ring Gen3 under real-world conditions throughout the pre-competition, competition, and post-competition phases of each event. The Olympic Games were the only event where sleep efficiency fell below the commonly used reference threshold of 85% during the competition phase accompanied by a reduction in the total sleep score and an increase in resting heart rate. The Olympic setting was accompanied by temporary changes in sleep and autonomic markers, but no sleep parameter or autonomic marker showed a statistically significant association with intra-individual competitive performance, although the limited sample size constrains the power to detect such relationships.

data.title_original: Finnish press and the societal issues of mega-sport events: a discourse analysis of Helsingin Sanomat’s coverage of the Barcelona 1992 and Paris 2024 Summer Olympics
data.abstract_original: Sports journalism has been criticized for ignoring sport’s social dimensions, but research suggests that those days of pure enthusiasm are over. This study inves­tigates how the Finnish press has covered societal issues in Olympic reporting and how this coverage has evolved over time. The data consist of Helsingin Sanomat’s coverage of the Barcelona 1992 and Paris 2024 Olympics. Societal issues were addressed in both cases, but the proportion of such articles was higher in 2024. Applying critical discourse analysis, the study examines the discourses through which the Olympics are rep­resented in these articles. Through discourse analysis, four discourses that both question and reinforce the legitimacy of the Olympics were identified. Coverage also includes highly critical reporting of the Olympic Movement. However, the comparison demonstrates a shift toward more critical, multi-voiced, and socially reflective sports journalism. Yet, national loyalty and the pursuit of Olympic success continue to temper its critical depth.
